text:
alex: quick RFC follow-up — we need an operator cutover playbook for moving customers from the shared peering mesh to per-tenant ephemeral-relays. primary goals: preserve customer-observed source IP when possible, avoid burst lease exhaustion during traffic surges, and provide fast rollback. looking for a concise ops checklist + exact operator commands we can run during a maintenance window.

mira: +1. add constraints: no double-nat paths, respect customer SNAT settings, and aim for <1min degraded path for controlplane API calls. also note RBAC / audit steps.

sam: sketch of phased approach: 1) pre-provision relay leases in target region (reserve pool) 2) warm-up: create relay with route + active health probes, advertise but keep traffic mirrored 3) shadow/sampling: route 5-10% of traffic to relay to validate 4) sticky cutover: move 100% traffic, keep sticky leases with TTL 10m to preserve srcip 5) reclaim: gradually free old shared peering leases.

sam: operator commands (examples):
```bash
# pre-provision 20 leases for customer cust-1234
curl -X POST https://ops.internal/egress-operator/v1/leases -d '{"customer":"cust-1234","count":20,"region":"us-west-2"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPSTOKEN'

# scale operators if under pressure
kubectl -n infra scale deployment/egress-operator --replicas=3
```

jordan: question — what if lease pool exhausts during a surge while we're shadowing? we need backpressure and an eviction policy: prefer short-lived non-sticky sessions, signal clients to retry idempotently, and auto-scale operator. also add a metric: lease_pool_available < 15% triggers autoscale.

alex: agree. failure modes & playbook snippets:
- lease_exhaustion: run `kubectl -n infra scale deployment/egress-operator --replicas=$(($(kubectl get deploy egress-operator -o jsonpath='{.status.availableReplicas}')+2))`, increase reserved pool for the affected customer, and if still failing, revert routing to shared-peering using route-group rollback id.
- healthcheck-failure on relay: mark relay CORDON, continue serving from shared-peering, schedule a replacement relay and re-run warm-up.

alex: minimal operator runbook (for on-call):
1) page #ops & #networking, set incident muting on prod alerts except lease_exhaustion.
2) run pre-provision command for affected customers.
3) start warm probes: `opsctl relay probe --customer=cust-1234 --relay=rel-usw2-12 --probe-count=100`
4) enable 5% sampling: `opsctl route modify --customer=cust-1234 --sample=5 --target=rel-usw2-12`
5) monitor `egress.lease_pool_available`, `relay.health` and `cp.request_latency` for 10-15m.
6) if stable -> `opsctl route promote --customer=cust-1234 --target=rel-usw2-12 --sticky-ttl=600`
7) if any metric breaks -> use `opsctl route rollback --customer=cust-1234 --to=shared-peering` and start postmortem.

mira: add audit steps: tag all commands with `--ticket=<INC>` and attach to customer timeline. auditors will want the route ids.

oncall-bot: ALERT: egress-operator lease_pool_low for cust-1234 (15:42 UTC). current_available=8 leases (threshold 10).

jordan: running through the checklist now in staging. one small nit: sticky-ttl 600s might be too short for long-lived websocket-ish flows. propose sticky-ttl 1800s for customers with long sessions, but we need a background refresh mechanism to extend leases.

sam: background refresh idea: implement lightweight lease-ping from relay -> `egress-operator` to extend sticky leases if session active. will add to RFC.

alex: decision for rollout cohort: start with low-risk customers (no long-lived sessions) and run two-phase cutover: cohort A (10 customers, 1% traffic), cohort B (50 customers, 10% traffic) across two weeks. ops tooling work: add `--sticky-ttl` per-customer override, and lease refresh endpoint.

mira: noted. action items: sam -> add lease-refresh API + metrics; jordan -> implement autoscale hook for lease_pool_low; alex -> write cutover playbook and merge into ops runbook doc.

oncall-bot: NOTE: incident created INC-2026-0452 for lease_pool_low (cust-1234). assigned to jordan.

alex: thanks — this is the follow-up I needed. documenting the exact commands above in the RFC reply. please keep replies short if you have concerns or blockers. :thumbsup:
